input.quote: 11.1 For Convenience. Customer may terminate this Agreement during the Term upon at least one (1) years' written notice to M&I, provided that Customer pays M&I an early termination fee ("Termination for Convenience Fee") in an amount equal to REDACTED of the Estimated Remaining Value.
input.rationale: The Term runs to the eighth anniversary of the Commencement Date (p0049), so a convenience exit is essential. Section 11.1 does give Customer a convenience right, but on one year's notice and against a percentage of Estimated Remaining Value (all remaining months' fees) plus unamortized Conversion costs and disposition Expenses, expressly outside the § 13.4 cap - far beyond the fallback's 60-90 days' notice and three-month fee ceiling, so it fails the fallback on material terms. On the M&I side, § 10.2 lets M&I withdraw any non-Core Service "at any time" on 90 days' notice, i.e. a mid-term partial convenience right; the 90-day notice already meets the fallback floor and is retained verbatim, so we only restrict the timing to the end of the Term. We target the fallback rather than preferred (notice stays at 90 days and we add no prepaid-fee refund) because deleting the Termination for Convenience Fee altogether would require collateral rewrites to the 50/50 payment mechanic, the § 11.2(A) cross-reference and the § 13.5 liquidated damages acknowledgement (p0208). The cap is achieved by the three-month formula plus deletion of the add-on costs sentence, with no further sole-remedy language. Favourable offsets are preserved (no fee on an M&I Event of Default, § 11.2(B); penalty-free Disaster exit, § 20.3), and the Termination for Cause Fee is left to its own rule.

proposal.summary: Cut Customer's convenience-termination notice to 90 days, cap the termination fee at three months' average monthly Fees, delete the unamortized-costs/Expenses add-on, and limit M&I's unilateral withdrawal of Services to the end of the Term.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a one-year notice period plus an uncapped exit charge on an eight-year term, so we move § 11.1 to our fallback: 90 days' notice and a Termination for Convenience Fee capped at three months' average monthly Fees, with the additional unamortized Conversion costs and disposition Expenses deleted. We also limit M&I's unilateral withdrawal of Services under § 10.2 to the end of the Term, retaining its existing 90 days' notice.

ops.oldText: upon at least one (1) years' written notice to M&I, provided that Customer pays M&I an early termination fee ("Termination for Convenience Fee") in an amount equal to REDACTED of the Estimated Remaining Value.
ops.newText: upon at least ninety (90) days' written notice to M&I, provided that Customer pays M&I an early termination fee ("Termination for Convenience Fee") in an amount equal to three (3) months of the average monthly Fees payable by Customer during the three-month period prior to Customer's notice.

ops.oldText: In addition to the foregoing, Customer shall pay to M&I, any unamortized Conversion or other costs, reasonable Expenses in connection with the disposition of equipment, facilities and contracts related to M&I's performance of the Services on behalf of Customer.
M&I may, at any time, withdraw any of the Services
ops.newText: M&I may, effective only at the end of the Term, withdraw any of the Services
